hook.en: A banyan tree is huge, yet it has no lungs and no blood. Still, every living cell in it takes in oxygen and gives out carbon dioxide. How does it manage?
hook.kn: ಆಲದ ಮರ ಬಹಳ ದೊಡ್ಡದು, ಆದರೂ ಅದಕ್ಕೆ ಶ್ವಾಸಕೋಶ, ರಕ್ತ ಯಾವುದೂ ಇಲ್ಲ. ಆದರೂ ಅದರ ಪ್ರತಿ ಜೀವಂತ ಜೀವಕೋಶ ಆಮ್ಲಜನಕ ತೆಗೆದುಕೊಂಡು ಕಾರ್ಬನ್ ಡೈಆಕ್ಸೈಡ್ ಬಿಡುತ್ತದೆ. ಹೇಗೆ?

objectives.en: Explain how plants exchange gases without special organs.
Define cellular respiration and respiratory substrates.
Trace glycolysis and count its ATP and NADH.

narration.en: A banyan tree is huge, yet it has no lungs and no blood. Still, every living cell in it takes in oxygen and gives out carbon dioxide. How does it manage?
narration.kn: ಆಲದ ಮರ ಬಹಳ ದೊಡ್ಡದು, ಆದರೂ ಅದಕ್ಕೆ ಶ್ವಾಸಕೋಶ, ರಕ್ತ ಯಾವುದೂ ಇಲ್ಲ. ಆದರೂ ಅದರ ಪ್ರತಿ ಜೀವಂತ ಜೀವಕೋಶ ಆಮ್ಲಜನಕ ತೆಗೆದುಕೊಂಡು ಕಾರ್ಬನ್ ಡೈಆಕ್ಸೈಡ್ ಬಿಡುತ್ತದೆ. ಹೇಗೆ?

body.en: Cellular respiration is the breaking of C–C bonds of complex compounds through oxidation within cells, releasing energy that is trapped as ATP, the energy currency of the cell. The compounds oxidised are respiratory substrates, usually carbohydrates, though proteins, fats and organic acids can be used in some plants under certain conditions. Plants have no specialised respiratory organs. Stomata and lenticels allow gas exchange; each plant part takes care of its own needs, there is little transport of gases from one part to another, and plants do not have great demands for gas exchange. Most living cells of a plant lie close to the surface, and the loose packing of parenchyma provides interconnected air spaces.

points.en: Respiration releases energy from food as ATP.
Stomata and lenticels allow gas exchange.
Roots, stems and leaves respire at far lower rates than animals.

narration.kn: ಜೀವಕೋಶ ಶ್ವಸನದಲ್ಲಿ ಆಹಾರದ C–C ಬಂಧಗಳು ಉತ್ಕರ್ಷಿತವಾಗಿ ಶಕ್ತಿ ATP ರೂಪದಲ್ಲಿ ಸಂಗ್ರಹವಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಸಸ್ಯಗಳಿಗೆ ವಿಶೇಷ ಶ್ವಸನ ಅಂಗಗಳಿಲ್ಲ; ಪತ್ರರಂಧ್ರ ಮತ್ತು ಲೆಂಟಿಸೆಲ್‌ಗಳ ಮೂಲಕ ಅನಿಲ ವಿನಿಮಯ ನಡೆಯುತ್ತದೆ.

body.en: Glycolysis (from Greek glycos = sugar, lysis = splitting) was worked out by Gustav Embden, Otto Meyerhof and J. Parnas, so it is also called the EMP pathway. It occurs in the cytoplasm of all living organisms and is the only process of respiration in anaerobic organisms. Glucose is phosphorylated to glucose-6-phosphate by hexokinase using ATP; fructose-6-phosphate is phosphorylated again with ATP to fructose-1,6-bisphosphate; this splits into dihydroxyacetone phosphate and 3-phosphoglyceraldehyde (PGAL). When PGAL is oxidised to 1,3-bisphosphoglycerate (BPGA), NAD⁺ is reduced to NADH + H⁺. BPGA → 3-PGA and PEP → pyruvic acid each give one ATP. So per glucose: 2 ATP are used, 4 ATP are made (net 2 ATP), 2 NADH are formed, and 2 pyruvic acid molecules result.

points.en: ATP used at two steps: hexokinase and the second phosphorylation.
Net per glucose: 2 ATP + 2 NADH + 2 pyruvate.

narration.kn: ಗ್ಲೈಕೋಲಿಸಿಸ್ ಅಥವಾ EMP ಪಥ ಜೀವದ್ರವ್ಯದಲ್ಲಿ ನಡೆಯುತ್ತದೆ. ಒಂದು ಗ್ಲೂಕೋಸ್ ಎರಡು ಪೈರುವಿಕ್ ಆಮ್ಲವಾಗುತ್ತದೆ; ನಿವ್ವಳ 2 ATP ಮತ್ತು 2 NADH ಉಂಟಾಗುತ್ತವೆ.

problem.en: Count the ATP balance of glycolysis for one glucose molecule.

steps.en: ATP used: 1 at glucose → glucose-6-phosphate and 1 at fructose-6-phosphate → fructose-1,6-bisphosphate: 2 used.
One glucose gives 2 triose molecules; each makes 1 ATP at BPGA → PGA and 1 at PEP → pyruvate: 4 made.
Net = 4 − 2 = 2 ATP, plus 2 NADH from the oxidation of 2 PGAL.

answer.en: Net 2 ATP and 2 NADH per glucose
